segments.text: Saving on autopilot may help you save more.
Payday arrives, the money gets spent, and whatever is left becomes your savings. Which is often nothing.
A 2001 study followed employees at one large company. When new hires were enrolled in a savings plan automatically, participation was significantly higher than when they had to sign up themselves.
A practical way to try this. One: pick a small amount. Two: schedule a transfer to a separate account on payday. Three: set it once, then leave it alone.
This was one study at one company, so results may differ for you. This is not financial advice.
Try it today: schedule one tiny transfer for your next payday.
